description: Probe-only evidence for hipkernel:flydsl_sdpa_cdna_decode (split-KV decode objects) on a padded leading stride, crossed with the declared alignment: BSHD or BHSD (layout), a small shape set, and a `pad` (0 to 31 elements) added to the row stride of the tensors `pad_on` names (q, k, v, o, or all four); the row stride is the stride between two consecutive sequence positions, in elements. BHSD: the row stride is the head size plus pad, and the head and batch strides grow with it. BSHD: the row stride is heads * head size plus pad and the head stride stays the head size, so a head's vector stays contiguous and only the rows are spread apart, the way a slice of a larger activation looks. The `pad` elements after a row are gap elements that belong to no element. `pad` takes 0 (packed), 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 (below or off a 16-byte vector of 8 half or bfloat16 elements), 8, 16 and 24 (16-byte multiples), and 9, 15, 17 and 31 (break the vector width). It is crossed with the declared alignment of Q, K, V and O (tensor_patches on uids 1, 0, 3, 2) and with the placement of the device pointers, as in Matmul/Align and SdpaFwd/Flash2: exact puts every device pointer at exactly the declared alignment, under misaligns Q below it (a PASS then means the backend rejected the pointer), default leaves the pointers where they are; under drawn at alignment 1 is rendered as exact. The FlyDSL CDNA kernels take every operand's batch, sequence and head strides as runtime arguments (not the fixed layouts of the rocKE dense kernel), so a padded row stride is a layout they can serve: servableStrides accepts a stride that is a positive multiple of 8 elements (the rows move as 16-byte vectors) with the head-dim stride 1 and the row stride at least the head size, and declines every other pad; the shared graph matcher also needs 16 bytes of declared alignment from Q, K, V and O. No mask, no stats, no bias; only strides, alignment and placement vary, the input fill stays at its default range. pad_on has no effect at pad 0, so every pad_on but 'all' is illegal there. `expect` is `declined` where the code says the graph cannot be served (a pad that is not a multiple of 8, a declared alignment below 16, and a pad on K or V alone) and `declined_or_pass` elsewhere, where the engine may take it and then must be right: WRONG or CRASH on a padded stride is the finding. Every claim is what the pack code says; no case of this space had been run on a device when it was written. The shapes are the decode kernel's, seqlen_q 2 to 8 and seqlen_kv 64 to 1024, head sizes 64, 128 and 256, grouped-query heads up to 8 per K/V head. With the padding on K or V alone (pad_on k or v, pad above 0) K's strides and V's differ, the graph needs an object that reads V through strides of its own, only a qk_mask object does and the decode catalog has none at these head sizes (its one qk_mask bucket is the MLA 1024), so the engine declines, whatever the pad.

derive.stride_q: [sq*row_q, d, row_q, 1] if layout == 'bshd' else [hq*sq*row_q, sq*row_q, row_q, 1]
derive.stride_k: [skv*row_k, d, row_k, 1] if layout == 'bshd' else [hkv*skv*row_k, skv*row_k, row_k, 1]
derive.stride_v: [skv*row_v, d, row_v, 1] if layout == 'bshd' else [hkv*skv*row_v, skv*row_v, row_v, 1]
derive.stride_o: [sq*row_o, d, row_o, 1] if layout == 'bshd' else [hq*sq*row_o, sq*row_o, row_o, 1]
derive.eff_placement: 'exact' if placement == 'under' and alignment < 2 else placement

constraints.reason: pad_on names no tensor when pad is 0: every pad_on would render the same packed graph

expect: ${'declined' if (pad % 8 != 0 or alignment < 16 or (pad > 0 and pad_on in ['k', 'v'])) else 'declined_or_pass'}
